description: Typed finite relation validation, sound bounded canonicalization and finite correspondence witnesses.
state: Named finite endpoint sorts, atom relations, contracts and exact Boolean matrices.
forward: Validate bounded typed formulas before evaluation.
Canonicalize with associativity, converse/complement commutation and converse pushed to atoms; minimum-height alphabetic chains keep canonical output within depth/node budgets.
Separate normalized formula match, finite coincidence, counterexample and incompatible contract.
Pure finite compositions retain endpoint, observation and assumption constraints and report univalence, converse univalence, totality, surjectivity and identity.
inverse: Converse preserves all antecedents within the declared finite table; no unique inverse claimed.
Complement uses the explicit inferred finite rectangle, not unsampled Rust behavior.
cost: Bounded O(nodes*64^2) matrix work plus AST labels, ordered normalization and an O(factors*height) chain memo; source IO and catalog enumeration delegated.
limitations: Finite formula models do not establish Rust correspondence.
Canonicalization is sound but incomplete; De Morgan and Boolean lattice laws are not used.
Converse/complement commutation and converse over union/intersection lack a Lean theorem.
No prose parsing, universal theorem proving, numeric approximation or stateful composition.
Caller must bound serialized input before allocation.
